one_liner: Podio has a free-to-use, broad REST-style API with OAuth2 (plus app-token auth) and webhooks, available on free accounts; an official MCP server is claimed but not verifiable from the provided pages.
auth_notes: OAuth server-side flow is the recommended method. For automated scripts, app authentication uses a special app token found in the app's developer info section (a static secret, so labelled API_KEY). Client API keys (client ID/secret) are self-generated from account settings, max 5 per user. Some destructive operations require an increased trust level via support request.
access_notes: Free and paid accounts have full API access at no extra charge within base rate limits (250/hr Limit A, 1000/hr Limit B). API keys are self-generated in account settings. Higher limits need a paid-plan API add-on. Some destructive operations are gated by trust level (support request).
blocker_notes: Base rate limits are modest and some destructive operations need a trust-level increase, but neither blocks a toolkit.

evidence.quote: The Podio API is available to use for both paid and free Podio accounts. Both have full access to the API
You have to [sign in or sign up](https://podio.com/home?force_locale=en_US) with Podio.
The recommended authentication method for the Podio API is the [OAuth server-side flow](https://developers.podio.com/authentication/server_side).
With app authentication you can authenticate as a single Podio app using a special app token.
The Podio API is a complete programmable interface to all Podio functionality.
you have the ability to register [webhooks](https://developers.podio.com/examples/webhooks) in your Podio apps
API keys include up to 250 API calls per hour for Limit A and up to 1,000 API calls per hour for Limit B.
